title: 持続可能性の確保（給付と負担）について (Securing sustainability: benefits and burden), Long-Term Care Insurance Subcommittee, 137th meeting, Document 1
date_evidence: 社会保障審議会 介護保険部会（第137回） 資料１ 令和８年10月26日
key_claim: The 20% co-payment line is pension and other income of ¥2.8 million or more for a single person (¥3.46 million for a couple); options lower it to between ¥2.6 million and ¥2.3 million (couples ¥3.26 million to ¥2.96 million); mitigation caps the increase at ¥7,000 a month for a period and lets those with savings at or below a set amount, ¥7 million, ¥5 million or ¥3 million for a single person (¥17 million, ¥15 million or ¥13 million for a couple), return to the 10% rate on application; the supplementary benefit already takes savings into account; a conclusion is due before the care insurance plan period that starts in fiscal 2027.
frame_summary: The ministry frames widening the 20% co-payment as a sustainability measure and presents the savings opt-back and the monthly cap as mitigation that protects low-asset users.

title: 第137回社会保障審議会介護保険部会 議事録 (Minutes, Long-Term Care Insurance Subcommittee, 137th meeting)
date_evidence: 2026-10-26 社会保障審議会介護保険部会（第137回）
key_claim: Members split on counting savings: Keidanren's member called taking savings into account appropriate; the care-manager association said savings alone have limits as a measure of ability to pay; the mayors' association doubted a savings condition could be a fair mitigation; the governors' representative said municipalities cannot check every institution, including online banks, or capture undeclared cash at home; the dementia family association said moving from 10% to 20% can add several hundred thousand yen a year.
frame_summary: The minutes record a council divided less over whether to widen the 20% charge than over whether savings can fairly or practically decide who pays it.

title: 76% of Economists Back Expanding 30% Medical Copayment to More Patients
